title: What Would Have Happened: Past Counterfactuals

sections.title: Reasoning about a past that did not happen
sections.content: You know *si hubiera tenido* from B1 Unit 35: *si* + *hubiera* + past participle imagines a past that did not happen, and *habría* + past participle says what would have followed. At B2 you use it to reason about causes and turning points, so three details matter. First, either clause can come first. Second, negatives are common in both clauses: *Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos ido al lago* tells you that it rained and that we did not go. Third, *si no hubiera sido por* + noun means "if it had not been for": it names the one thing that made the difference.

sections.title: Reading a past counterfactual
rows: Si hubiera salido antes, habría llegado a tiempo.
If I had left earlier, I would have arrived on time. (I did not leave earlier, and I was late.)
Habría llegado a tiempo si hubiera salido antes.
The same meaning with the result clause first.
Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos ido al lago.
If it had not rained, we would have gone to the lake. (It rained, so we did not go.)
Si no hubiera sido por tu ayuda, no habría terminado.
If it had not been for your help, I would not have finished.

items.spanish: Si hubiéramos salido más temprano, habríamos llegado antes del concierto.
items.english: If we had left earlier, we would have arrived before the concert.

items.spanish: El proyecto habría terminado a tiempo si el equipo hubiera tenido más ayuda.
items.english: The project would have finished on time if the team had had more help.

items.spanish: Si no hubiera sido por el mapa, nos habríamos perdido en la montaña.
items.english: If it had not been for the map, we would have got lost in the mountains.

sections.content: *Habría* never goes after *si*: say *Si hubiera salido*, not *Si habría salido*. Each half of the sentence looks at the past: the next lesson shows a second form for the result clause.
